title: Mittag-Leffler modules descend faithfully flatly
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and let $M$ be an $R$-module. If $S\otimes_R M$, with $S$ acting on the first factor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], is a Mittag-Leffler $S$-module [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], then $M$ is a Mittag-Leffler $R$-module. No flatness, countable-generation or finite-presentation hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05A5, lemma-ffdescent-ML; the source writes M tensor_R S, canonically isomorphic by swapping factors to S tensor_R M.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-module-finitely-presented-directed-colimit], choose a small nonempty directed partially ordered set $I$, finitely presented $R$-modules $M_i$, transition maps $f_{ij}$, and a colimit identification $M=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}M_i$ with canonical maps $f_i:M_i\to M$.

source.place: Tag 058G, theorem-lazard proof, finitely presented colimit presentation

proof.text: Tensoring this presentation with $S$ gives the directed system $(S\otimes_RM_i,S\otimes_Rf_{ij})$ of finitely presented $S$-modules with colimit $S\otimes_RM$: finite presentations remain finite after scalar extension, and tensor product commutes with the displayed directed colimit. Since $S\otimes_RM$ is Mittag-Leffler by hypothesis, [lem-trf-mittag-leffler-eventual-domination] gives, for each $i$, an index $j\ge i$ such that $S\otimes_Rf_{ij}$ dominates $S\otimes_Rf_i$.

source.place: Tag 05A5 proof, first paragraph invoking Proposition 059E after tensoring the finitely presented colimit

proof.text: Fix $i$ and the corresponding $j$. Let $N$ be the pushout of $f_i:M_i\to M$ and $f_{ij}:M_i\to M_j$, with canonical map $g:M_j\to N$. Tensoring the pushout square with $S$ gives the pushout of $S\otimes_Rf_i$ and $S\otimes_Rf_{ij}$, because scalar extension is a tensor-product left adjoint and therefore preserves this colimit. The pushout relation is the same after the canonical identifications.

source.place: Tag 05A5 proof, pushout diagram and sentence 'tensorization by S ... is a pushout diagram'

proof.text: The domination obtained in Step 2 and the pushout description in Step 3 allow [lem-trf-domination-pushout-universal-injective] to conclude that the base-changed map $S\otimes_Rg:S\otimes_RM_j\to S\otimes_RN$ is universally injective over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM applied to the pushout in Tag 05A5

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-faithfully-flat-universal-injective-reflection] to the faithfully flat map $R\to S$ and the $R$-linear map $g:M_j\to N$. Since its scalar extension is universally injective by Step 4, $g$ is universally injective over $R$.

source.place: Tag 05A5 proof, final sentence 'using that R -> S is faithfully flat we conclude ... universally injective'

proof.text: By [lem-trf-domination-pushout-universal-injective] again, universal injectivity of the pushout leg $g$ implies that $f_{ij}$ dominates $f_i$. This holds for every $i$ with a suitable $j\ge i$, so the converse direction of [lem-trf-mittag-leffler-eventual-domination] proves that $M$ is Mittag-Leffler over $R$.

proof_origin.place: Algebra Tag 05A5, lemma-ffdescent-ML proof; supporting Tags 058G, 059E and 0AUM
